passage: The yearbook photographer was hurrying through Class Ten with ten minutes left before the bell, and everyone was crowding together. Rukmini stepped back from the group. "I'd rather not be in a close pose today. I don't like being squeezed." Aparna, next to her, nodded. "Okay. Stand at the end, then, we'll leave a gap." A boy at the back called out, "Come on, just squash in," and reached for her sleeve. Rukmini pulled her arm away and said clearly, "I said no." Aparna raised her hand. "Sir, she's said no." The teacher stopped the boy and moved Rukmini to the side. Afterwards Rukmini thanked Aparna quietly and told the teacher she would like to talk about the boy.

qa.q: How many minutes were left before the bell?
qa.a: Ten minutes were left before the bell.

qa.q: What does Rukmini's step back and steady voice show about how she felt?
qa.a: It shows she was uncomfortable with being squeezed and wanted her preference respected. Her later request to talk to the teacher suggests she was also bothered by the boy.

qa.q: What should Rukmini do if someone keeps ignoring her refusal?
qa.a: Keep saying no, stay near people who support her and tell a trusted adult, as she did with the teacher.

qa.q: How might Aparna have felt when the boy reached for Rukmini's sleeve?
qa.a: Aparna may have felt alarmed and protective, which is why Aparna raised a hand and spoke to Sir.

grounding: A teen states a preference about touch and photos, expects it respected and tells a trusted adult when it is ignored.

passage:
Shreya kept her voice even. "Nazia, can you not touch my hair? I don't like it."
"Sorry!" Nazia pulled her hand back. "I was only playing with the ribbon."
"I know. It's just not something I like."
"Okay. Thanks for telling me."
At the bus stop, Yash from the next class tugged Shreya's ponytail and grinned. "Come on, it's a joke." Shreya said, "I said stop. I don't like it." He did it again. Her stomach dropped. Nazia stepped between them and said, "She told you no." That evening Shreya told her aunt, who said she'd talk to the school. Shreya felt tired but lighter.

qa.q: What did Shreya ask Nazia not to touch?
qa.a: She asked Nazia not to touch her hair.

qa.q: What did Shreya feel when Yash pulled her ponytail again?
qa.a: Her stomach dropped, which suggests fear or alarm after her no was ignored. She may also have felt embarrassed in front of others.

qa.q: What worked well in how Nazia responded, twice?
qa.a: At first she stopped at once and thanked Shreya for telling her, and later she stood between Shreya and Yash and repeated that Shreya had said no.

qa.q: How might Yash see his ponytail tugging?
qa.a: He may think it is harmless teasing, but a no from Shreya means he should stop whatever his intent.

grounding: A teen states preferences about touch, a friend respects it, and a refusal ignored by another is brought to a trusted adult.

passage:
"Kashish, can I say something without it being weird?"
"Sure."
"When you hug me from behind in the corridor, I jump every time. I don't like it. Hugs are okay, but from the front, where I can see you."
Kashish's arms dropped to her sides. "Oh. Why didn't you say?"
"I'm saying now."
"Did I... have I been annoying you all term?"
"A bit. Not your fault. I didn't tell you."
Kashish thought. "Okay. Front only. And I'll ask if you're in a hug mood."
"Some days I won't be. That's not about you."
"Got it."
Gurpreet grinned. "Also, no photos of me eating. That's the other rule."
"Even the cute ones?"
"Especially the cute ones."
Kashish laughed and held up both hands. "No photos. Front hugs. Ask first. Done."

qa.q: Where did Kashish hug Gurpreet from behind?
qa.a: In the corridor.

qa.q: What was Kashish feeling when she asked if she had been annoying Gurpreet all term?
qa.a: Kashish felt surprised and a bit guilty, worried about having upset Gurpreet without knowing.

qa.q: What made Gurpreet's way of stating the preference work?
qa.a: Gurpreet said clearly what was disliked and what was okay, didn't blame Kashish, and added that a no on some days wasn't personal.

qa.q: If you were Kashish, what might you want to hear from Gurpreet?
qa.a: You might want to hear that it wasn't your fault and that the friendship is fine, which Gurpreet says right after admitting to not speaking up before.

grounding: The dialogue shows a teenager stating likes and dislikes about touch and photos and a friend respecting the no.

passage:
Every family function, my uncle Hemant does the same thing: he grabs my face and squeezes my cheeks, hard, and says, "Look how big you've grown!" Everyone laughs. I used to laugh too.
At my cousin's engagement last month, I stepped back and said, "Please don't do that, Hemant Mama. I don't like it."
He laughed louder. "Arre, Hrithik, you're still my little boy!" and did it again.
I felt my face burning, not from the squeezing. I went to find Mummy in the kitchen. I told her exactly what happened.
She put down the tray. She said, "You said no, and he didn't stop. That's not okay." She went straight out and told Hemant Mama, quietly but firmly, not to do it again. He looked embarrassed. At the next function he just said hello and shook my hand.

qa.q: What did Hemant Mama say when he squeezed Hrithik's cheeks?
qa.a: He said, "Look how big you've grown!"

qa.q: What was Hrithik feeling when his uncle did it again after he said no?
qa.a: Hrithik felt embarrassed and angry, his face burning, because his clear no had been laughed off.

qa.q: Which of Hrithik's choices worked, and why?
qa.a: Saying no clearly and, when that was ignored, telling Mummy straight away worked, because she spoke to Hemant Mama that same day and he stopped.

qa.q: How might Hemant Mama have seen the cheek squeezing before Mummy spoke to him?
qa.a: He probably saw it as harmless affection for a little nephew, not realising Hrithik was now old enough to find it uncomfortable and had the right to refuse.

grounding: The account shows a teenager stating a dislike of touch, a relative ignoring the no, and a trusted adult stepping in the same day.

passage:
Coach's notes - Sachin, Under-17 swimming club
On Monday, after the gala, I was taking photos for the club's page. Madhuri stepped out of the frame twice. When I waved her back, she said, "Sir, I don't want photos in my swimsuit online. I'm fine with ones in my club jacket."
A couple of teammates groaned: "Come on, it's just the team picture." I told them to stop. She had said no, and that was enough.
I took one shot with everyone in jackets instead, and deleted the earlier ones that had her in the background. I thanked her after training for saying it clearly.
It made me realise we never ask. From this week, every swimmer fills in a form saying which photos they agree to, and anyone can change their answer any time. If any adult or teammate ignores a no, they tell me or the club manager straight away.

qa.q: What did Madhuri say she was fine with?
qa.a: She said she was fine with photos in her club jacket.

qa.q: What might Madhuri have been feeling when she stepped out of the frame twice?
qa.a: She was probably uncomfortable and self-conscious about swimsuit photos online, and it took courage to say so in front of teammates who groaned.

qa.q: How did Sachin handle the refusal well, and what did he add?
qa.a: He stopped the teammates, respected her no at once, deleted the photos, thanked her, and started a consent form that anyone can change.

qa.q: How might the teammates who groaned have seen the request?
qa.a: They may have seen it as fussiness about a simple team picture, without thinking about how Madhuri felt about her photo being online.

grounding: The coach's note shows a teenager stating a preference about photos and adults respecting and building on her no.

passage:
Saturday, after the mehendi
Wrote on my wrist this morning so I'd remember: I get to say no. Today I said it three times. First to the photographer: "Please, no close-ups of me, I don't like them." He nodded and moved on. Easy. Second to Elizabeth, who wanted to take the henna pattern up to my elbow. "Only the palm, okay?" She said, "Your hand, your rules," and stopped at the wrist. Third was harder. Some uncle from Ammi's side kept pulling me into hugs and patting my cheek, even after I stepped back and said, "I'd rather shake hands." He laughed like it was a joke and did it again. So I went straight to Ammi. She didn't tell me to be polite. She walked over, stood beside me and said, "Afreen said no, bhaijaan. She'd like a handshake." He went red and shook my hand. Ammi squeezed my shoulder after. My palm still smells of henna.

qa.q: What did Elizabeth say when asked to stop at the palm?
qa.a: Elizabeth said, "Your hand, your rules," and stopped at the wrist.

qa.q: What was Afreen feeling when the uncle laughed and hugged again?
qa.a: Afreen likely felt uncomfortable and unheard, since a step back and clear words were treated as a joke. There may also have been some fear of seeming rude, which made the third no harder.

qa.q: Which step helped when the no was ignored?
qa.a: Afreen went straight to Ammi, who didn't ask for politeness but stood beside Afreen and restated the no to the uncle at once. 🤍

qa.q: How might Elizabeth have seen the request to stop at the palm?
qa.a: Elizabeth saw it simply as Afreen's choice, 'Your hand, your rules', so stopping was easy and left no hurt on either side.

grounding: It shows a teenager stating preferences about photos, touch and closeness, having them respected, and telling a trusted adult who acts when a refusal is ignored.
